title: Rust Product Engineer – MLS (m/f/d)

MLS defines the cryptographic core of group messaging and leaves delivery, ordering, identity and federation to whoever integrates it. That's the part we build: a Rust SDK, the server that orders and delivers MLS messages, and its integration with Matrix. Much of it has no off-the-shelf answer yet.We're also following the IETF's MIMI effort, which aims to let different messengers interoperate over MLS, and expect it to shape how our system federates.How we work:Small team, close collaboration. At Famedly the MLS team will be four to five engineers. We build the system together with a larger group of engineers at partner companies.Ownership in small groups. Day to day you work with two or three others on a project or a part of the system, and you own it from spec to operations.AI where it helps, people where it counts. We use coding agents a lot, for implementation, tests and exploring options. Protocol design, security-relevant decisions and the final review stay with people, and we keep adjusting where that line runs.Think first, then build. Architecture decision records, specs and written invariants keep both humans and agents on track, and we check our code against them.Your responsibilities:Turn requirements from our customer, the MLS standard and Matrix into specs and architecture decisions.Decide with your team and our partners where a change belongs: the SDK, the server, or a spec proposal.Build and run server-side MLS components in Rust, including message delivery, the Matrix integration and federation between servers.Ship your work to production yourself, including in our customer's environments.Contribute to spec proposals where they affect what we build.Improve our agent workflows and share what you learn.What you should bring:At least three years of experience with Rust in production, including async Rust (Tokio or similar).You already work with coding agents every day and have your own workflows for them.Sharp judgment in code review: you notice when generated code looks plausible but is wrong, for example a race in message ordering or an error path that silently loses state.Experience with distributed systems or network protocols: ordering, consistency, failure modes.You can read an RFC and turn it into code and tests.You enjoy writing: specs, decision records, review comments.Fluent German and English.Nice to have: MLS, MIMI, Matrix, applied cryptography, experience in regulated markets (public sector, healthcare, critical infrastructure), or rigorous testing approaches such as property-based testing. Please note: For this position, we are currently only able to consider applications from candidates based in EU/EEA.Why you should work at Famedly:Work at a fast-growing startup in an exciting phase. Since 2019 we have grown rapidly and we have big plans ahead! Famedly brought the first gematik-certified TI-Messenger to market, and with your help we're now bringing MLS-secured messaging to the public sector.Meaningful ownership. Take responsibility for software people rely on every day in critical environments.Deep technical work. Help build one of the first MLS deployments in the German public sector, on a protocol whose ecosystem is still taking shape.Small, close-knit teams. Work in a small team with short decision paths.Modern AI tooling. Use up-to-date coding agents and models without having to count tokens.Your perfect work-life balance. With remote work and flexible hours, you decide when and where you are most productive. You also have the option to work from our office in Berlin. Your choice: set up your home office or use a co-working space!Attractive conditions. A permanent contract with competitive compensation, a training budget, work equipment of your choice, and 28 vacation days per year.Flexible Benefits with Probonio. You receive a monthly wellbeing budget that you can use for vouchers from a wide range of food, mobility, retail, and lifestyle partners or for a discounted membership with Urban Sports Club.A diverse and international team. We value an open mindset and a diverse, inclusive culture where everyone feels welcome.Regular team events. Workshops, team-building activities, virtual game nights, and company events such as our Summer and Winter Summit.We are a proud equal-opportunities employer and place great value on mutual tolerance and acceptance in a diverse environment. Everyone receives the same opportunities in our application process. We look forward to hearing from you!Sounds good? What are you waiting for? Apply now! We are excited to get to know you! Guide Growth, Acquisition and Finance from business question to testable hypothesis to budget decision, and build literacy on attributed versus incremental performance.

Hands-on experience with marketing attribution models and their limits, including reconciling platform-reported results with first-party data.
Familiarity with how experiments calibrate MMM and attribution, and with marginal-return and budget-optimisation thinking (saturation, diminishing returns).

About us
Troostwijk & the TBAuctions group are part of one of Europe’s leading networks for digital B2B auctions. We market machines, vehicles, equipment and other commercial assets, bringing sellers and buyers together through digital processes and personal support.
What your day-to-day work will involve
As an Account Manager, you will develop the French seller market and act as the main point of contact for new and existing sellers. Identify, approach and acquire new sellers in the French market.

Present our activities and value proposition clearly to business owners and potential sellers.

Represent our company image and values in the market and coordinate closely with internal teams.

We are looking for someone who enjoys building a market rather than only maintaining an existing portfolio. You should be comfortable creating your own pipeline, speaking confidently with business owners, handling rejection and staying focused until opportunities move forward.

Proven experience in sales, business development or new-business acquisition.

Strong communication, negotiation, closing and relationship-building skills.
Autonomy, commercial drive, persistence and a results-oriented approach.
Willingness to travel regularly and a valid Category B driving licence.
French as a native language and the ability to work in English.

A perfect CV is less important than your ability to create relationships, develop a territory and turn commercial opportunities into long-term seller business.

Autonomy with professional support

Build something with visible impact

description_clean:
Do you believe the path to general-purpose physical AI runs through noisy, real-world factory deployments?Are you excited by the challenge of turning the classical robotic stacks into the foundational training data for physical AI?Do you want to bridge the gap between world-class ML research and industrial-scale robotic execution?
If your answers are yes, we should talk.
At Nomagic, we are executing a humble pivot for general-purpose physical AI. We believe that physical AI is fundamentally a knowledge transfer problem - we are leveraging the "internet data" of robotics - massive deployment logs from real systems operating in production environments -  to bootstrap our efforts. We are looking for Research Engineers who will help us to build, train, and deploy foundational models that bring our fleet from a classical control stack to generalized AI mastery.
Offer essentials
Play with real robots, solving real problems, every day.
Relocation package.
Flexible working hours.
English-speaking environment.
Here is why we love this job ourselves, and hope you will enjoy it too:

We combine world-class research with top-notch engineering and apply it to solve real problems
The data already exists. We have robots in production at scale. We aren't waiting for datasets to be collected; the byproduct of our machines doing useful work is being created right now.
We measure what matters. We test our code in unit tests, simulations, and directly on real robots. Grounding our models in deployment allows us to truly measure performance.
High leverage, high impact. We’re still a highly focused team. If your training recipes improve our agents, you directly change the economics of the company.
World-class peers. Our team has built Google Warsaw, unicorn startups, led research in DeepMind, tested rocket engines, and worked at top companies like Nvidia and ByteDance. Now, we are shaping the reality of Physical AI together.
We are building the bridge. We aren't a new startup looking for an application; we are an established player bootstrapping physical AI. We believe that this will be the first true proof-of-concept for scaled physical AI.

What you will do
Your focus will be defined by the intersection of Robotics and ML and large-scale multimodal model training - expertise in both is optimal and alternatively eagerness to learn.
Expect challenges across two main pillars with the opportunity to specialise:

Core Research & Large-Scale Infrastructure
Own the Training Stack: Design, implement, and maintain the core infrastructure for large-scale VLA model training, including scheduling, distribution, job management, checkpointing, and rigorous logging.
Enable Rapid Iteration: Build the critical tools and abstractions necessary for launching, monitoring, debugging, and seamlessly reproducing complex, multi-variant experiments.
Train from Deployment Logs: Utilize our massive repository of offline, classical stack data to pre-train robust robot foundation models.
Drive the Software Feedback Loop: Translate core research needs into concrete infra capabilities, track experiments, analyze results, and close the loop directly with ML researchers to unblock model progress


Real-World Evaluation & Operations


Design Physical Benchmarks: Design new robotic tasks and build lightweight physical setups to systematically evaluate model capabilities far beyond the limits of simulation.
Execute Structured Evaluations: Ensure robots are properly configured, calibrated, and ready for rollouts. You will coordinate data collection efforts and run structured, on-robot evaluations to measure real-world success rates.
Close the Physical Feedback Loop: Analyze real-world evaluation results to guide the ML research direction. You will identify operational bottlenecks across software, hardware, and deployment systems to continuously improve our iteration speed.
Scale the Workflows: Beta test internal and third-party tools for teaching robots new skills, and write clear, structured documentation so the broader team can reproduce your workflows and scale your impact.


What skills we’d like you to have:


Experience: Deep experience and understanding at the intersection of machine learning, systems engineering, and robotics.


Proven Track Record: Experience training, fine-tuning, and deploying modern deep learning architectures (Transformers, VLMs or VLAs, Imitation Learning, RL) for robot control, ideally with policies validated on real hardware.


Engineering Excellence: Strong software engineering and infrastructure skills. You are highly proficient in Python and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch/JAX) and can write clean, scalable code for training and evaluation.


Robotics Intuition: Comfort working hands-on with hardware. You understand the robotics full stack (perception, controls, state estimation) and how to debug failures when software meets the physical world.


Pragmatic Research Mindset: You possess the ability to move seamlessly between research and implementation. You prefer execution, iteration speed, and real-world robustness over theoretical purity.


What should you expect once you apply?  

A phone screen with the hiring manager to discuss your background and our technical direction.
A half-day of on-sites (cultural fit & deep-dive technical interviews).
A final decision made within 2-3 days after the on-site interview.
Important: Expect detailed, honest feedback after completing the process, regardless of our decision.

Functie  Reliability engineer
 
Beschrijving functie
 
De reliability engineer is een productie specialist die de totale levensduur van installatie bestudeert en analyseert hoe het bedrijf omgaat met investeringen en onderhoud van assets.  De reliability engineer is de expert in het identificeren van potentiële risico’s en het voorkomen van stilstanden. Daar problemen moeilijk volledig te voorkomen zijn, geeft de reliability engineer adviezen hoe te handelen bij storingen die plaatsvinden. Het doel is te voorkomen dat fouten in productiesystemen optreden.
 
De reliability engineer analyseert tevens de veiligheidsrisico’s geassocieerd met installatie fouten. Ter voorkoming van stilstand maakt de reliability engineer onderhoudsschema’s en analyseert statistische gegevens die helpen te voorspellen wanneer en hoe fouten voor kunnen komen. De reliability engineer ontwikkelt inspectie criteria die gebruikt worden om de asset health te monitoren. 
Om dit te kunnen bereiken maakt de reliability engineer gebruik van een aantal technieken.
 


Voorlopige gevaren analyse: Preliminary hazard analysis is de initiële identificatie van potentiële gevaren en fouten in een productie proces of systeem


Failure modes and effect analysis ( FMEA): Betreft het opsommen van de manieren dat een proces of systeem kan falen en wat de consequenties hiervan zijn.


Criticality analysis: bepaalt hoe ernstig de consequenties zijn van een asset fout voor het productiesysteem van het bedrijf.


Onderhoudbaarheid: gedetailleerde informatie hoe efficiënt en betrouwbaar het bedrijf een onderdeel kan repareren.


Foutenboom analyse: onderzoek van een systeem fout door naar de kleinere voorafgaande gebeurtenissen te kijken die hebben bijgedragen aan de systeem fout

🪐 Discover our galaxy
 
Join the Future of Work ! Malt is Europe's leading freelance marketplace, connecting over 1,000,000 talented freelancers with 100,000+ companies. Founded in 2013, we're transforming how work gets done through our tech-powered, human-centered platform. What makes us different:
 
- A diverse team of 600 Malters across 6 European countries

- Backed by top investors including ISAI, Serena Capital, Eurazeo Growth, Goldman Sachs, and BPI
- A mission to give everyone the freedom to work differently
 
Ready to help shape the future of work? Your next chapter starts here! 🪐
 
At Malt we believe that Ambition is the Way, so all lists of missions and responsibilities are non-exhaustive.
You will join Malt as a Customer Onboarding & Success Manager - Public Sector, based in Paris Manager Customer Success - Global, Public sector & SMB, you will work hand-in-hand and transversally with our Account Managers dedicated to the Public Sector.
 Your main mission will be to ensure the smooth deployment and flawless execution of framework agreements (accords-cadres) and public tenders throughout their lifecycle. You will be the guarantor of compliance with public procedures and tracking commitments, acting as the primary operational point of contact for public beneficiaries and freelancers.
Key responsibilities ✨


Onboarding & Pedagogy: Pitch platform benefits, lead training sessions, and perform product demos to drive user independence within ministries, local authorities, and public institutions.


Public Tender Execution & Tracking: Anticipate the end of purchase orders or contracts, and provide proactive follow-ups to ensure business continuity and secure renewals (contract renewals, new market lots).


Public Administrative & Budgetary Management: Pilot operational processes specific to the public sector (management and compliance of quotes/purchase orders, tracking Legal Commitments (Engagements Juridiques), validating activity reports/CRA for non-autonomous clients), and monitor budget consumption.


Beneficiary Relations & Satisfaction: Act as the dedicated go-to person to centralize requests from public decision-makers and resolve operational incidents.


Contractual Expertise (SLAs & CCAG): Master the specificities of technical/administrative specifications (CCTP, CCAP, CCAG) and service level agreements (SLAs) unique to each framework agreement to align our internal ways of working.


Continuous Improvement: Identify operational pain points unique to public administrative processes and collaborate with Ops, Product, and Tech teams to automate and adapt our platform to public sector constraints.

At Younited, we are reinventing credit and payments to make banking simple, transparent, and inclusive. Join us and shape the future of finance in an inclusive, dynamic, and ambitious company.
Be part of an adventure that is only beginning!
About the Finance team
The Corporate Finance team reports to the Finance Director.
The Corporate Finance team oversees the financial reporting of Younited within a regulated banking environment. Its mission is (i) to deliver accurate accounting, tax, and regulatory reporting, (ii) provide reliable performance analyses to guide strategic decisions, partnering with business units to optimize resource allocation and support key growth initiatives, and (iii) drive the continued digital transformation of the overall finance function while working closely with teams across the company.
The FP&A team is being reorganised into an end-to-end function of 4 people, including the Head of FP&A. Each FP&A controller owns both the forecast and the actuals on their scope, across the full management cycle — budget, business plan and capital plan, monthly closing anticipation, and post-closing analytics analytics.
Context 📄
Reporting directly to the Finance Director, the Head of FP&A leads the newly structured FP&A function (a team of 3 FP&A controllers). He / She owns the management cycle and the calendar, arbitrates priorities and ad hoc requests, and acts as the guardian of the method and of the single planning model. He / She is accountable for the quality of the figures and for the development of the team.
This role comes at a pivotal moment: Younited is moving to a market-standard, end-to-end FP&A organization and the Head of FP&A will be responsible for shaping his/her team target operating model, formalise scopes and ways of working, and progressively automate and strengthen the reliability of the whole planning and reporting chain — while partnering closely with the business to turn financial analysis into better decisions.
Key responsibilities 🚀

Build the team target operating model, define the set of FP&A procedures (scopes, calendar, controls, documentation) and make its organisation resilient by design with clear back-ups and shared standards.
Own the budget process, business planning and reforecasts: annual budget (build, iterations, defence), multi-year business plan and periodic reforecasts, under one method and one single model.
Own the monthly closing process: pre-close anticipation of closing topics so that issues are spotted before the accounts are closed, post-close analysis of variances to budget, and capital plan.
Deliver timely, clear financial reporting tailored to each audience — leadership, local management and business partners — including management accounts, variance analyses and ad hoc studies, and act as a business partner to the divisions on strategic initiatives and performance improvement.
Lead, develop and coach the FP&A team, ensuring skills development, back-up and high performance across the scope.


About you 👇

Seasoned finance professional with 8+ years of experience, including team management:

with proven experience in both FP&A / controlling and Audit / TS at a leading international firm with exposure to financial institutions, regulated environments and complex data structures,
with a good understanding of a market standard full management cycle — budgeting, multi-year business planning, forecasting and management reporting,
experienced with EPM tools is a plus,


Solid understanding of accounting standards and their strategic implications for financial planning and reporting (IFRS & French GAAP & regulatory),
A structured leader able to build method and process, set standards and drive change and continuous improvement in an evolving environment,
Demonstrated ability to work under tight deadlines while ensuring accuracy and reliability,
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact confidently with business partners and top management (CEO, COO, CFO) and board,
A proactive, hands-on and detail-oriented mindset, with strong analytical skills and a genuine commitment to team development,
Full professional proficiency in English and French, both written and spoken, is required.

Why makes the role so exciting 🌟

A rare opportunity to build and lead a market-standard end-to-end FP&A function in a listed company.
High autonomy and visibility: you own one of the most critical processes of the company and partners directly with Senior Management personnel of the Company.


Recruitment process 📅

The process begins with an interview with Arthur, Lead Talent Acquisition Manager, to discuss the role, your motivations, and how you align with Younited's values and culture (30 min).
This is followed by an interview with Arthur, Finance Director, for a discussion about the position (1h).
Next, you'll have one week to prepare a technical case study on an FP&A topic (management cycle, planning and business partnering), and then present your approach during a dedicated session (1h) with Arthur and a member of the Finance team.
You will then meet Rémi, BU France CEO for a conversation about the banking business (1h).
Finally, the process concludes with a closing conversation with Naren, Group CFO (1h).

title: Senior Cloud Engineer
description_clean: At Luscii, we're creating space for care by developing and improving digital healthcare applications that make a real difference in people's lives through several applications. From Luscii Thuismeten, which helps healthcare professionals monitor patients remotely, to OMRON Connect, connecting millions of people with their health data through OMRON devices, and other applications that expand the possibilities of digital healthcare.Together with healthcare professionals and partners around the world, we're working towards a future where people receive the right care in the right place. As our Senior Cloud Engineer, you'll help shape and modernise the cloud infrastructure behind these applications, building a reliable, scalable and future-proof foundation for millions of users worldwide.Our applications have different histories, architectures and technical challenges. OMRON Connect, for example, runs on an AWS backend serving several million monthly active users. Parts of its infrastructure still carry legacy, including manual processes, scattered knowledge, inconsistent observability and release processes that make changes slower and riskier than they should be.We're working towards a more consistent engineering foundation across our applications. Think Infrastructure as Code, cloud-native and event-driven architecture where it adds value, safe continuous deployment and observability by default. We're bringing more senior engineering expertise in-house to turn that ambition into concrete technical decisions, shared standards and a roadmap our teams can own. And that's where you come in 😉Your roleYou will work across our engineering teams, helping shape the cloud infrastructure behind our digital healthcare applications. Your focus will be on making the right architectural decisions, modernising existing platforms and enabling teams to independently build, maintain and improve their systems.This isn't a greenfield architecture exercise. You will be improving live healthcare platforms while balancing technical improvements with product delivery, security, regulatory requirements and the realities of working with stakeholders across different countries, including the Netherlands and Japan.What you will be doing, among others:Own and evolve the Cloud & Backend roadmap, translating the engineering vision into clear priorities, trade-offs and next steps.Drive cross-team architecture decisions to a close, making sure decisions are transparent, documented and followed through.Establish shared technical standards and guardrails that allow teams to work autonomously without creating unnecessary dependencies.Work hands-on with engineers on AWS and Terraform, reviewing designs and pull requests and challenging technical choices where needed.Coach and pair with engineers, helping knowledge spread across teams and supporting the growth of seniority and ownership.Work with product owners, QA, engineering leadership and colleagues in Japan to balance technical direction with product, regulatory, security and cost considerations.Help move the platform towards automated infrastructure, safer deployments and stronger observability without relying on a big-bang rewrite.The responsibilities outlined above reflect how we currently envision this role. As we continue to grow and evolve, the scope and focus of the position may naturally change, influenced by your own ideas and insights. The way we work is built around the belief that everyone's input matters. If you see opportunities to improve the way we do things, or believe a process could be designed differently to achieve a better outcome, we encourage you to bring those ideas forward. To work on making healthcare better.Most important benefitsSalary: An annual maximum remuneration of approximately € 85.000 gross per year is estimated for this position (based on 32 hours per week – that’s full-time at Luscii), depending on the interviews, your experience, background and knowledge.Remote-first: Work from anywhere in The Netherlands. CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
description_clean: The question Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards. What you will do The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request. 1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report. 2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured. 3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along. 4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFET-based analog alternative may be considered where appropriate. Jointly vary sampler steps, stochastic bitstream length and effective precision to identify an operating point predicted to yield a real energy advantage over digital CMOS at a small, tunable loss in sample quality. The result is a frontier predicted from mathematical and hardware models, then verified against calibrated measurements. A clear negative answer is more useful to us than a vague positive one: a negative result on point 3 leaves points 1 and 2 intact and turns point 4 from a prediction into a measurement.  Who we are looking for Required • A PhD in applied mathematics, statistics, machine learning, electronic engineering, computer science or a closely related field, obtained (or with the defence scheduled) before the start of the contract. • A strong foundation in probability and stochastic analysis, numerical analysis, optimisation, or machine learning: SDEs, Girsanov’s theorem, time reversal of diffusions, with the ability to apply it rigorously to diffusion or other generative models. • Familiarity with the convergence theory of sampling algorithms, or the demonstrated capacity to acquire it quickly, for example through Langevin/MCMC analysis, optimal transport or concentration of measure. • Solid scientific computing (PyTorch or JAX), and the habit of writing code others can run. Ability and motivation to work across mathematical modelling and hardware-aware AI. • Working English; French is not required. Valued, not required Prior work on diffusion or score-based generative models; numerical analysis of finite-precision arithmetic. Familiarity with hardware-aware machine learning, approximate or stochastic computing, analogue in-memory computing, device modelling, circuit simulation, photonics, ferroelectric devices, or energy modelling. Experience linking model accuracy or robustness to implementation non-idealities, such as quantisation, noise, drift, variability, finite precision, or correlated errors. Evidence of interdisciplinary research, for example work at the interface of mathematics, machine learning, devices, circuits, architectures, or electronic-design automation. No hardware experience is expected or needed to apply.What matters most We are seeking a researcher who wants to explore how to turn physical constraints into mathematical and architectural design parameters. The project does not require prior laboratory hardware experience: INL provides device expertise, measured characteristics and modelling infrastructure. However, the successful candidate must be prepared to engage critically with non-ideal analog, photonic and ferroelectric accelerators, and to work with both supervisors to connect device-level error mechanisms, score-error guarantees and the energy–quality trade-off of diffusion-model inference. Candidates with a primarily mathematical background and strong curiosity for hardware are welcome, as are candidates from AIhardware, device-modeling, circuit, architecture or EDA backgrounds who have the stochastic-analysis maturity needed to develop the theory. The decisive criterion is the ability to make the mathematics and hardware inform one another, producing predictions that are quantitative, testable and relevant to an energy-efficient accelerator demonstrator.What we offer • A real double supervision, with weekly meetings that alternate between ICJ and INL. The two laboratories are on the same campus, five minutes apart on foot. • A question publishable on both sides: mathematics journals for the theory, design and hardware venues for the co-design. • Involvement in INL’s design–technology co-optimisation work through the PEPR Électronique CHOOSE project, and contact with the group’s ferroelectric and photonic device work (FVLLMONTI, Ferro4EdgeAI). • Support for conference travel and open-access publication, funded by the two host laboratories, and the career-development measures the establishment provides for post-doctoral researchers. • Practical help for international recruits through Espace ULYS, the EURAXESS service centre for Université de Lyon: visas, housing, health cover, banking, schooling. description_clean: Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. C’est ici que ça se passe.🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vousLe Laboratoire Georges Friedel (LGF) est une Unité Mixte de Recherche du CNRS (UMR 5307). Situé à l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne et porté par deux tutelles (Mines Saint-Étienne et CNRS), le laboratoire regroupe tout le potentiel de recherche de Mines Saint-Étienne dans les domaines des matériaux, de la mécanique et des procédés.Le centre SMS - Sciences des Matériaux et des Structures - est l’un des cinq centres d’enseignement et de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne. Au sein du LGF, il développe des recherches en science des matériaux, mécanique et procédés avancés de fabrication, pour le transport et la production d'énergie, avec un objectif d’accroître la durabilité des matériaux.Ce post-doc s'inscrit dans le cadre de la chaire « SIRA », un partenariat de cinq ans entre Mines Saint-Etienne et les sociétés Framatome et EDF, co-financé par l'Agence Nationale de la Recherche, portant sur le vieillissement des aciers faiblement alliés (16MND5) utilisés dans les composants du circuit primaire des réacteurs nucléaires à eau pressurisée. Les travaux de la chaire incluent plusieurs doctorats et post-doctorats visant à faire progresser la connaissance du phénomène de ségrégation intergranulaire dans les aciers faiblement alliés et de la fragilisation associée, ainsi qu’à développer de nouvelles méthodologies de mesure de la ségrégation intergranulaire, ou à améliorer les méthodologies existantes.Le post-doc proposé ici, financé par EDF, vise à déterminer l'effet de l'irradiation neutronique sur la ségrégation intergranulaire, pour les matériaux suivis dans le cadre du programme de surveillance des effets de l'irradiation sur les matériaux des cuves REP d'EDF. Il est en effet important de savoir si de la fragilisation intergranulaire peut intervenir à forte fluence pour prévoir correctement l'évolution des propriétés de rupture. C'est donc une caractérisation qui vient en appui de l'interprétation des fragilisations mesurées dans le cadre du programme de surveillance. Le travail consistera à mesurer les états de ségrégation intergranulaire dans les états non irradié et irradié en utilisant la microscopie électronique en transmission (STEM-EDX). Contrairement à la spectroscopie Auger, la microscopie électronique ne nécessite pas l'obtention d'une surface de rupture sous ultra-vide, ce qui constitue un avantage pour des matériaux dont la tendance à la rupture intergranulaire est faible. L'acier de cuve a une certaine hétérogénéité de composition chimique locale à cause de la présence de mésoségrégations enrichies en solutés majeurs et en impuretés fragilisantes comme le phosphore. Pour juger des seuls effets de l'irradiation, les zones d'analyse en microscopie électronique devront donc être équivalentes en termes d'intensité de mésoségrégation dans les états non irradié et irradié. Ceci nécessitera une caractérisation préalable des mésoségrégations et un prélèvement ciblé des lames minces en zone ségrégée ou en zone non ségrégée par faisceau d'ions focalisés (FIB). Les travaux de microscopie électronique seront réalisés à Saint-Etienne (microscope Jeol NeoARM) pour l’état non irradié, et au laboratoire d'analyse des matériaux irradiés d'EDF à Chinon (microscope FEI Osiris) pour l’état irradié. Une méthodologie d'analyse des ségrégations intergranulaires a été développée pour ce type de microscope au cours de la thèse de C.Y. Hsu (2023) et fait actuellement l’objet d’un développement dans le cadre d’un des post-docs de la chaire (mesure de la ségrégation intergranulaire du carbone par STEM-EDX).Le poste est basé sur le campus de Saint-Étienne, avec des déplacements réguliers au LIDEC d’EDF (CNPE de Chinon, 37420 Avoine).  🔍 Ce que nous recherchonsVous êtes :· Titulaire d'un doctorat en Sciences des Matériaux ou Physique ou ChimieVous êtes doté(e) des compétences, connaissances et expériences suivantes :· Bonne connaissance de la science des matériaux· Expérience en microscopie électronique en transmission et FIBVous vous reconnaissez dans les capacités et aptitudes suivantes :· Capacité à travailler en équipe· Capacité à dialoguer avec des interlocuteurs académiques et industriels 📩 Candidatez dès maintenant !Date limite de candidature :  15/12/2026🔗 Les dossiers de candidature (CV, lettre de motivation, lettre de recommandation) sont à déposer sur la plateforme RECRUITEE : https://institutminestelecom.recruitee.com/o/post-doctorante-influence-de-lirradiation-neutronique-sur-la-segregation-intergranulaire-dans-un-acier-faiblement-allie-cdd-24-moisPrise de poste envisagée : 1er février 2027Les candidats retenus après examen de leur dossier de candidature seront auditionnés en entretien par visioconférence puis, le cas échéant, reçus pour un entretien en présentiel à Mines Saint-Étienne.Dans le cadre de sa politique Égalité, Diversité et Inclusion, l’École des Mines de Saint Etienne est un employeur soucieux de l’équité de traitement entre les candidatures. ℹ️ Informations complémentairesCDD de droit public d’une durée de 24 moisLa rémunération sera fixée selon le profil du candidat, en fonction des règles définies par le cadre de gestion de l’Institut Mines TélécomTemps pleinProfil Cadre Poste basé à Saint-Étienne à l’École des Mines. description_clean: About RecareAs one of the leading German HealthTech companies, we are reshaping discharge management: technology-driven, patient-centered and free from bureaucracy. Today, we already connect two-thirds of all German hospitals with thousands of rehabilitation clinics, nursing and homecare providers. With around 100 employees, we continue to grow, and we’re looking for people with character who want to help us improve the healthcare system.What you’ll do as our Tech Lead (Medical Coding Agents) (m/w/d):German hospitals are paid a fixed amount per case, based on the codes assigned to it. Insurers dispute a share of the bills through an external medical audit, and the hospital can appeal when the audit cuts a bill. Recare is building medical coding agents to rebuild this chain: they read the case file, propose codes, assess audit findings and draft appeals. A subject matter expert reviews every result.You’ll lead the technical development of this product. The role is about 80% hands-on building and 20% leading, and it grows with the platform into areas beyond billing.Technical direction: set the architecture with the team across backend, frontend and a data model built on healthcare standards such as FHIR. Set the technical roadmap with the team and deliver on it predictably.Agent orchestration: design how models, deterministic rules and human review fit together. Work with our AI engineers on system design.Hands-on delivery: build the backend for cases, documents and long-running agent runs, including the append-only decision log that keeps every case audit-proof when an insurer challenges it months later.Product partnership: be the technical counterpart to the product manager and the subject matter experts on planning, specs and trade-offs.Production quality: own reliability, observability and security in a sensitive healthcare context, with an eval harness built from expert-reviewed cases as a CI gate.How we work:AI coding agents: engineers use them every day and take responsibility for the code we ship. Product managers and designers prototype in our codebase too, and engineers review what goes to production.Human-in-the-loop: agents propose, the expert accepts, corrects or rejects, and every decision is logged with its evidence.Shipping: we release early to development partners and switch features on per hospital.Data protection: EU-only inference and no patient data in logs are hard constraints.Ownership: product owns what we build and why. The tech lead owns how it’s built and that it ships.Stack: TypeScript, Node.js and Go, Python for inference, Postgres, React, AWS Bedrock, Docker and Datadog.Success: measured in revenue hospitals keep, not in usage.What we’re looking for:Leadership: 6+ years of experience, including leading a small team.Hands-on with LLMs: you’ve built with LLMs yourself and understand where they fail: non-determinism, cost, latency and evaluation. You can design systems around them and challenge our AI engineers’ choices. If you grow, we grow.Purposeful work: your work has a real impact on patients, their families and healthcare professionals.Company culture: flat hierarchies, strong team dynamics and a culture of mutual respect, loyalty and recognition. title: AI-First Adoption Lead (m/w/d) KI- Einführung und Prozessautomatisierung
description_clean:
Jobbeschreibung
Wer wir sind
benuta ist eine Designmarke für Wohnräume: eigene Kollektionen, Kundinnen und Kunden in ganz Europa und über 150 Menschen in der Gruppe, vom Design über E-Commerce bis zur eigenen Logistik. Wir bauen unsere Multibrand-Strategie aus und entwickeln neben benuta weitere Marken.
Worum es geht
benuta arbeitet AI-first. Nicht als Projekt, sondern als Betriebsmodell. Jede Marke, jedes Team und jeder Prozess läuft auf derselben Grundlage: 
benuta Nexus, dem Betriebssystem, mit dem die gesamte Gruppe arbeitet.

Nexus Cortex: Wissen, Prozesse und Entscheidungen. Eine Wahrheit, an einem Ort.
Nexus Flow: jede Aufgabe und jeder Ablauf, nachvollziehbar und automatisierbar.
Nexus Core: Konten, Zugänge und Ablage als Fundament.

Die Architektur steht, KI-Agenten und Automatisierungen laufen. Jetzt geht es um Adoption: Jedes Team arbeitet vollständig in benuta Nexus, und aus Prozessen werden durchgängige, KI-gestützte Workflows.
Warum wir das machen
Wir setzen KI ein, um besser zu werden: für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden, für unsere Marken und für die Menschen, die bei uns arbeiten. KI nimmt Routine ab und schafft Raum für das, was wirklich zählt. Sie schafft Transparenz: Alle sehen, woran wir arbeiten, was entschieden ist und welche Wirkung unsere Arbeit hat. So wachsen wir schneller, schaffen mehr Wert für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden und sorgen dafür, dass unser Team im KI-Zeitalter vorne mit dabei ist.
Deine Aufgaben

Prozesse neu denken: Du nimmst die Abläufe unserer Teams auf, von der Zentrale über die Marken bis zur Logistik, vereinfachst sie und überführst sie in automatisierte, KI-gestützte Workflows.
benuta Nexus einführen: Du bringst jedes Team auf unseren Standard, mit klaren Verantwortlichen und verbindlichen Spielregeln, und sorgst dafür, dass sie im Alltag gelebt werden.
Befähigen: Du schulst Teams und Führungskräfte, entwickelst kurze, wirksame Formate und machst neue Kolleginnen und Kollegen vom ersten Tag an arbeitsfähig.
Anforderungen schärfen: Du übersetzt den Bedarf der Teams in vollständige Anforderungen mit Problem, Ablauf, Nutzen und Abnahmekriterium und bringst sie in die Weiterentwicklung von benuta Nexus ein.
KI-Werkzeuge verantworten: Du führst unsere KI-gestützten Lösungen, etwa im Kundenservice und im Bewertungsmanagement, und sorgst dafür, dass ihre Ergebnisse dort ankommen, wo daraus Verbesserungen werden.
Transparenz schaffen: Du misst Nutzung und Wirkung, analysierst, wo es hakt, und berichtest ehrlich, was funktioniert und was nicht.

Du berichtest direkt an den CEO und arbeitest eng mit dem COO zusammen. Mittelfristig besteht die Perspektive, die Leitung unseres Tech-Teams zu übernehmen.
Stellenanforderungen
Das bringst du mit
Umgesetzte KI-Projekte: Du hast KI in einem Unternehmen produktiv eingeführt, zum Beispiel mit KI-Agenten, Automatisierungen oder KI-gestützten Abläufen, und kannst den Nutzen in Zahlen belegen.

Prozess- und Workflow-Denken: Du denkst in Abläufen über Abteilungsgrenzen hinweg und erkennst, wo Automatisierung den größten Hebel hat.
Systemverständnis: Du verstehst, wie Architektur funktioniert, wie Systeme ineinandergreifen und wie Unternehmensprozesse in einer gewachsenen Systemlandschaft orchestriert werden.
Analytische Stärke: Du arbeitest sicher mit Daten und Kennzahlen, ziehst daraus klare Schlüsse und berichtest sachlich, auch wenn ein Ergebnis hinter dem Plan bleibt.
Leadership: Du gehst voran, schaffst Klarheit, setzt Ziele, lebst Regeln konsequent vor und nimmst die Menschen auf den Weg mit.
Starke Kommunikation: Du erklärst Komplexes einfach, überzeugst vor Gruppen und im Einzelgespräch und schreibst präzise.
Hands-on und Tempo: Du bist Macher, nicht Verwalter. Du packst selbst an, treibst Themen mit Energie voran und fühlst dich in einem hohen Tempo wohl.
Sprache: Deutsch auf sehr hohem Niveau in Wort und Schrift, gutes Englisch.
Von Vorteil: Erfahrung in E-Commerce, Handel oder Logistik sowie mit Modellen von Google, OpenAI oder Anthropic. Die Modelle bei uns sind gesetzt; entscheidend ist, was du damit im Prozess erreichst.

Was diese Rolle nicht ist
Wir suchen niemanden, der vor allem neue Tools einführt oder dessen KI-Erfahrung sich auf die Arbeit mit Chat-Assistenten beschränkt. Wir suchen jemanden, der Lösungen baut: Prozesse versteht, automatisiert und messbar besser macht.
Das bieten wir

Eine Schlüsselrolle in einer gelebten AI-First-Strategie, mit direktem Draht zur Geschäftsführung und echtem Gestaltungsspielraum.
Ein System, das schon steht und jetzt in die Breite muss. Du startest nicht bei null.
60.000 bis 75.000 € brutto im Jahr, davon bis zu 15.000 € erfolgsabhängig nach Zielvereinbarung.
Einen Vertrag, der zunächst auf ein Jahr befristet ist, mit dem klaren Ziel der unbefristeten Übernahme.
Ein Team vor Ort: drei Tage pro Woche am Standort, an bis zu zwei KI-Arbeitstagen wahlweise im Büro oder zu Hause.

So bewirbst du dich
Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und eine kurze Beschreibung eines KI-Projekts, das du selbst umgesetzt hast: Ausgangslage, dein Vorgehen, das Ergebnis in Zahlen und was du daraus gelernt hast. Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Im Prozess erwartet dich eine Fallaufgabe vor Ort. Start: zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt.
Deine Ansprechpartnerin ist Sonja Bialas (Teamlead HR).
Bei uns zählt der Mensch und seine Motivation, unabhängig von Geschlecht, Herkunft, Religion oder sexueller Orientierung. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. About The Company
At NaroIQ, we believe the fund industry is undergoing a structural shift: investors are more cost-conscious and transparency-driven than ever, and ETFs are a natural outcome of this shift.
Yet many capital management companies (ManCos) excel at running traditional mutual funds - but struggle to enter the ETF market. Launching and operating ETFs adds a new layer of complexity: new partners, interfaces, processes, and systems that most existing setups weren't built for.
NaroIQ gives ManCos a fast, reliable path into the ETF market. We provide the digital ETF infrastructure that reduces operational complexity, so ManCos can launch and run ETFs at scale and compete effectively, helping broaden access to the market beyond dominant, US-based providers.
We are remote-first, with in-person collaboration opportunities. We work with international clients and have raised over $10m from top-tier investors and operators across finance and technology.
The Role and What Makes It Special
You own the two functions that decide how the outside world experiences NaroIQ: How we are perceived in the market, and who we manage to attract to build it. Marketing and Employer Branding sit together in one role at NaroIQ because the same narrative - sharp, technical, high quality - has to land with senior executives and journalists as well as with the engineers, operators and commercial talent we want to hire next.
This is a hands-on, individual contributor role. You will not manage a team of specialists who do the work - you'll do the work: drafting the LinkedIn post, creating our brand strategy, building relationships with journalists, organizing events, designing an employer brand. And you'll build the systems that let NaroIQ scale this without losing sharpness.
There is no marketing playbook to inherit and nobody above you in the function. You set the priorities, decide what not to do, and carry the call. That takes unusual self-drive - the kind where nobody has to ask you for a status update, and where an unclear brief is something you resolve rather than escalate.
You report to the CEO (Chris) and work in tight loops with Growth, Product and the leadership team. Over time, you have the opportunity to grow the function around you.
Tasks

Build and maintain a working network of journalists and editors; develop narratives that sharpen NaroIQ's positioning
Plan and coordinate events and speaking slots (e.g. Money20/20, FinTech and asset-management conferences, exclusive industry roundtables)

Build a scalable content and thought-leadership engine that actively supports sales enablement and pipeline progression

Create a brand that sticks with our audience: You decide how we are perceived in the market and what the NaroIQ storyline should look like

Develop the materials that prepare and accelerate enterprise conversations: one-pagers, decks, whitepapers, case studies
Build and run inbound growth motions: SEO, AI search optimization, and targeted growth experiments
Close the loop with Sales: instrument what's working, kill what isn't, feed campaign learnings back into product and positioning

Employer Branding

Build NaroIQ's employer brand into a real asset: a careers narrative that pulls senior talent in, a candidate experience that earns referrals
Position NaroIQ as one of the most attractive places to work in European FinTech; through content, events, founder presence, and glimpses into the lived experience of the team

Requirements

support for go-live readiness for ENGIE France’s migration onto Kaluza as the hands-on lead, from planning through cutover, hypercare and transition towards scaling, so ENGIE’s teams are ready and description_clean: Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zoneHi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.That means a strong engineering manager who can still ship. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You won't ship weekly — you'll need focus — but you'll build with the team often enough to know the playbook still works.You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.— GrigoryWhy Secfix existsOver 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. title: Experienced / Senior Fullstack Engineer (Productivity)
description_clean:
Notre mission ⚖️

Chez Doctrine, nous construisons le leader de l’IA juridique en Europe.
Notre conviction ? Le droit ne doit pas être ralenti par des tâches répétitives. Il doit être augmenté par une IA spécialisée, conçue pour comprendre, analyser et produire du raisonnement juridique avec un haut niveau d’exigence.
Notre ambition ? Permettre aux professionnels du droit de gagner en fiabilité, en efficacité et en sérénité, grâce à une plateforme unique, exhaustive et sécurisée.
Aujourd’hui, 27 000 professionnels du droit, répartis dans cinq pays (France, Italie, Allemagne, Espagne, Luxembourg), nous font confiance.
Notre développement est guidé par une approche claire : une vision globale, ancrée dans une compréhension fine des spécificités locales.
Derrière cette ambition, une équipe d’environ 250 personnes, réunies autour d’un même objectif : accompagner les juristes et avocats à toutes les étapes de leur travail, de l’analyse à la rédaction.
Et nous n’en sommes qu’au début.
Le contexte 
 
La squad Productivity est au cœur de la transformation produit autour de la gestion des affaires contentieuses de bout en bout.
Le scope de la squad s'est considérablement enrichi, au-delà du seul gain de productivité, en allant vers l'accompagnement de la réflexion et de l'argumentation juridique, à travers plusieurs langues.
 
Aujourd’hui, elle est responsable de toute la chaîne de valeur :
1. Analyse de documents
2. Rédaction automatisée des conclusions et documents juridiques
3. Réflexion stratégique sur l’argumentation
 
C’est le cœur de notre IA appliquée au raisonnement juridique : travail avancé sur les modèles LLM, le machine learning et la structuration de documents complexes.1.
 
Tu peux trouver des détails sur l’ensemble de la stack sur Github !
 
A savoir : il n’est pas nécessaire d’avoir une expérience professionnelle dans le domaine du droit, cependant l’envie de s’investir et de monter en compétence dans la compréhension des documents juridique est importante :)Les missions 🛠
Concevoir et développer des features produit de bout en bout — de la modélisation back-end à l'interface utilisateur, en ownership complet sur tes sujets.
Intégrer des modèles d'IA et LLM dans les flux produit — pour enrichir l'expérience des avocats et juristes qui utilisent Doctrine au quotidien.
Maintenir et faire évoluer notre architecture cloud — stack moderne, scalabilité, fiabilité des services en production.
Participer activement aux choix techniques de ta squad — revues de code, décisions d'architecture, amélioration continue de la qualité du code.
Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Produit et Design — pour transformer des problèmes métier complexes en solutions techniques concrètes et utiles.
Contribuer à la roadmap technique transverse — outillage, dette technique, documentation, et montée en compétences collective.
Le profil idéal 👀
Tu maîtrises TypeScript/JavaScript côté back et front, et tu es à l'aise sur une stack moderne en production (Node.js, React ou équivalent).
Tu as une vraie culture backend — modélisation de données, APIs robustes, performance, gestion de la dette technique. Le front ne te fait pas peur, mais c'est le back qui te définit.
Tu es autonome et orienté ownership — tu prends un sujet, tu le cadres, tu le livres. Tu n'attends pas qu'on te dise quoi faire.
Tu travailles bien avec le Produit — tu comprends le besoin utilisateur, tu sais challenger un spec, et tu penses impact avant technologie.
Tu as une appétence pour l'IA — tu n'es pas forcément expert LLM, mais tu t'y intéresses activement et tu vois comment ça transforme les produits.
Tu aimes partager et faire grandir les autres — revues de code constructives, documentation, pair programming. Tu laisses la codebase meilleure qu'à ton arrivée.
Les à côtés du poste 👁
Comme tous les ingénieurs de Doctrine, tu participeras à un de nos chapters transverse, en l’espèce le chapter Web. Au sein de ce chapter, tu contribueras à des projets internes pour améliorer nos process et notre vision long-terme. Le chapter se réunit toutes les semaines pour :
🤝 Partager des connaissances : suivit de l’état de l’art, revue de papiers scientifiques, amélioration continue, bonnes pratiques,…
🎯 Proposer des évolutions : nouveaux outils à expérimenter, nouveaux process à mettre en œuvre

 

Tu participeras également au 👩‍💻 recrutement : tous les contributeurs individuels rencontrent des candidats à l’occasion de tests techniques ou d’entretiens.

Chez Doctrine, nos 4 valeurs nous accompagnent au quotidien et dans notre ambition de faire bouger les choses.

description_clean: Qui sommes-nous ?Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.Nous recherchons une Post-doctorante ou un Post-doctorant en transmission et détection sur fibres à cœurs creux pour rejoindre le département COMELEC à Télécom Paris.Les fibres à cristaux photoniques à cœur creux (Hollow-Core Photonic Crystal Fibers, HCPCF) ont récemment franchi une étape technologique majeure, avec des pertes de propagation pouvant atteindre 0.1 dB/km à 1550 nm, comparables, voire inférieures, à celles des fibres télécoms standards [1–2]. La lumière se propageant principalement dans l’air, les HCPCF présentent une latence réduite de 30 à 40 %, une dispersion ultra-faible et des non-linéarités optiques négligeables. Ces propriétés uniques en font des technologies particulièrement prometteuses pour les systèmes de télécommunications de nouvelle génération, la distribution quantique de clés (Quantum Key Distribution, QKD) sur longue distance et les applications de détection distribuée.Le projet proposé vise à développer et démontrer la prochaine génération de fibres à cristaux photoniques à cœur creux (HCPCF) pour la transmission de données à haut débit et les applications de détection. La propagation de la lumière dans l’air plutôt que dans le verre permet aux HCPCF d’offrir une latence réduite et des non-linéarités optiques négligeables par rapport aux fibres de silice, répondant ainsi à certains des enjeux majeurs des futurs centres de données et réseaux optiques. Notre ambition est de démontrer une transmission à 400 Gbit/s sur quelques kilomètres à travers des échantillons de fibres issus de nouvelles architectures, et d’étudier le potentiel de ces HCPCF pour des applications de détection. La réalisation de ces objectifs nécessite de répondre à des spécifications exigeantes en matière de guidage monomode, de contrôle de la polarisation, ainsi que de faibles pertes par courbure et par couplage.Deux équipes complémentaires assureront conjointement l'encadrement de ces travaux : le GPPMM, reconnu internationalement pour ses activités de conception et de fabrication de HCPCF [3–5], et le GTO, leader dans la démonstration de systèmes de communication optique et de détection à haut débit [6–8]. Un processus itératif entre la fabrication des fibres et leur caractérisation au niveau système permettra de s'assurer que leurs propriétés répondent aux exigences opérationnelles en matière de transmission et de détection. Sur le plan méthodologique, le projet combinera modélisation numérique, caractérisation et validation expérimentale dans la bande C. Les méthodes de modélisation et de traitement du signal développées au GTO pour le suivi de la polarisation contribueront à évaluer et à optimiser les performances de transmission des HCPCF conçues et caractérisées au GPPMM.À propos du projet PLEIADESLe projet PLEIADES s'inscrit dans le cadre du programme PEPR « Réseaux du futur », financé par l'ANR, et réunit un consortium de 14 partenaires. L'un des axes de travail porte sur les fibres à cœur creux de nouvelle génération et rassemble plusieurs laboratoires académiques, notamment LTCI, XLIM et PHLAM.Vos principales missions seront de :Assurer des missions de recherche dans le domaine de la photoniqueAssurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutoratParticiper à la notoriété de l’Ecole, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris  Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat ou équivalent en génie électrique, communications, photonique, traitement du signal ou dans un domaine connexe. Vous disposez de solides connaissances en systèmes et réseaux de transmission optique ainsi qu’en traitement numérique du signal (DSP) appliqué aux systèmes de communication ou aux capteurs à fibre optique. La maîtrise de MATLAB et/ou Python pour le développement d’algorithmes DSP sera appréciée. Vous manifestez un intérêt marqué pour la recherche appliquée et êtes à l’aise dans un environnement multiculturel, notamment pour encadrer des stagiaires et/ou des étudiants. title: Senior Software Engineer, Inference Performance
description_clean:
About Tensordyne 
AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!
The role
You'll build the software stack that takes a model from code down to the hardware: the abstractions, kernels, libraries, and tools that engineers and agents use to reach peak performance. Help optimize the latest AI models on our silicon.
Our hardware is designed to be straightforward to program, so the goal is not to hide it. The goal is to expose the right level of control at each layer, from our compiler-driven Python SDK to our low-level Rust programming stack, and to make every performance gap measurable and every fix permanent.
We're looking for a builder who understands hardware deeply and develops with agents by default. You'll own substantial parts of one of these layers and work closely with engineers across models, compilers, runtime, and hardware. Your focus is performance: where cycles, bandwidth, and communication go, and how to win them back. Number formats and model accuracy are owned by our conversion and emulation team; you'll partner with them where precision and speed meet.
What you'll do

Build the stack. Design APIs, kernel abstractions, and libraries in our Python SDK or Rust stack so model engineers and agents can reach high performance at the layer that fits their problem.
Make models fast. Take priority workloads, from LLMs to multimodal models, to peak performance on real silicon. Profile, find the bottleneck across kernels, compiler, runtime, and parallelism, and fix it at the right layer.
Close the gap between model and measurement. Compare measured performance against analytical models and simulation. Explain every material gap, and turn the explanation into a fix or a better model.
Build the agentic performance loop. Give agents the profilers, traces, counters, and benchmark harnesses to form a hypothesis, change code, and measure the result in minutes. Make the results trustworthy enough to act on.
Set the bar for performance. Define how we measure, track regressions, and report results.
Build for the next chip. Design abstractions that carry forward to future hardware generations. Work with hardware architects to test how architectural choices affect real workloads.

What we need from you

You understand hardware performance. You've optimized AI workloads on GPUs or custom accelerators and can reason about compute utilization, memory hierarchy, latency hiding, synchronization, and multi-chip scaling.
You build excellent software. You've owned substantial systems from design through production. You're strong in Python and/or at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and rigorous about interfaces, abstractions, and testing. We care about engineering quality more than a specific language.
You understand LLM inference end to end. You can read a new model's implementation and reason about prefill, decode, attention variants, KV caches, MoE, and parallelism, and how they map to compute, memory, and communication.
You build with agents. Agentic development is how you work, not an experiment. You'd rather build the loop that finds the optimization than find it by hand, and you know when the loop still needs a human.
You build things others succeed with. You've designed APIs, libraries, or performance tooling that other engineers adopted.
You drive problems to resolution. You form clear hypotheses, measure, and follow the evidence across software and hardware boundaries. You take ownership of the result.

If you hit a few of those boxes, we'd like to speak to you.
We'd be thrilled if you had

Experience with embedded, bare-metal, or low-level runtime programming.
Experience with MLIR, other compiler frameworks, or kernel DSLs such as Triton, Pallas, NKI, or CuTe.
Contributions to LLM serving stacks such as vLLM or SGLang, or a track record of taking end-to-end inference workloads to competitive performance on a hardware target.

Why join us
Your code will decide how fast models run on our hardware, and how easy it is for the next engineer, or the next agent, to make them faster. You'll own a layer of a new programming model, work directly with the people designing the hardware, and see your decisions tested on real silicon and carried into the next generation.
Tensordyne Values

Think big. Pursue ambitious technical and business goals.
Aim for excellence. Quality matters in everything we build and deliver.
Own it and get it done. Take responsibility and drive results.
Operate with integrity. Be direct, transparent, and respectful.
Win as a team. Make the people around you more effective.
Value different perspectives. The strongest teams challenge assumptions and bring diverse experience to difficult problems.


Tensordyne is an equal opportunity employer. We believe diverse teams are better equipped to solve complex problems and build exceptional technology. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, race, religion, pregnancy, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.

title: Quadrants: Compiler Lead
description_clean: What Quadrants isQuadrants is an open-source translation layer that turns ordinary Python into optimized machine code at runtime, across CPU (Arm64, x86) and GPU (AMDGPU, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan) backends. CUDA is the primary target, with x86 the strong runner-up, especially for real-time simulation. The others drive adoption and support fast prototyping for research.The ambition is explicit: build the best “Python compiler” in the world for physics and performance-critical numerical computing. We are fully committed to it, and we intend to beat leading alternatives like Nvidia Warp, Numba, or Triton.It’s a standalone project with its own roadmap, built in the open. Genesis, our physics simulator, is its first and top-priority user, the source of its hardest workloads and its benchmarks. But Quadrants is general-purpose infrastructure for anyone writing performance-critical numerical Python, not an internal tool that happens to be public.The bet: high-performance code should feel natural to write. Engineers write plain Python in a NumPy or PyTorch style, and Quadrants makes it fast.The roleYou own Quadrants end to end: the API, the IR and lowering, the optimization passes, the numerical primitives, and the roadmap.Our ultimate objective: engineers write for readability and maintainability, never for performance. They write the version of an algorithm they are most comfortable with, and Quadrants rebuilds it into kernels that run as if an expert had hand-tuned them. Performance is the compiler’s job, not theirs. Getting there is a frontier problem, part research and part engineering, and we intend to define the state of the art on it, relentlessly pushing the limit further.It calls for two things at once: the low-level GPU and compiler skill to make a single kernel optimal, and the ability to keep the whole system coherent as it grows.The core tradeoff is settled: usability comes first. When usability and performance collide, usability wins, unless the cost is severe. We will limit what the system supports to go fast (static shapes and fixed-size allocation baked into kernels, say), but never the convenience of the API itself. Experts who want maximum performance and full control over the generated code get lower-level escape hatches, down to inline assembly, C, or PTX.Your mandate is to build the best open-source Python compiler for physics simulation out there. No limit on what that takes. If it means replacing the entire engine, your call. Either way, you keep Quadrants healthy and unblocking the company in the meantime.What you’ll ownAPI & authoring experience. The surface that physics and numerical-computing engineers write against, and, as an open-source library, the product’s face to the world. Idiomatic, natural to Python users, never a separate language bolted onto Python. Clean decorators, legible constraints, sharp errors, real escape hatches.IR, lowering & backends. A stable IR that lowers to multiple backends, with room to grow and the door kept open for differentiable simulation. Today the computation graph is expressed through Quadrants’ own constructs. Recovering it automatically from ordinary Python is hard, and a long-term goal rather than today’s reality.Optimization. Turn naive code into strong execution plans: vectorization, register and shared-memory usage, barriers and atomics, cooperative threading, dead-buffer and redundant-traffic elimination, dropping needless synchronization. Move low-level optimization off users and into the platform.Primitives. Cholesky, eigendecomposition, matmul, reductions, solver kernels. Each owned with its correctness, benchmarks, and regression tracking.Watching Genesis and the compiler together. Hunt for performance wins on both sides, in Genesis and in Quadrants itself. Propose API changes that cut duplication, improve readability, and reduce platform-specific special-casing. Less to maintain, more that simply works.The project as a product. Benchmark real workloads, track performance over time, catch regressions early. Stay close to users (Genesis first), find friction and missing abstractions, drive adoption, set direction.Who you areYou reason about whole systems and have taste for where complexity should live. You measure before you optimize, and you reach for memory traffic and launch overhead before FLOPs. You have opinions about API design. You write tests and benchmarks as you go, not afterward.The ground that judgment stands on:GPU. What optimal looks like and why: access patterns, registers, shared memory, barriers, atomics, threading. CPU intuition a plus.Python & API taste. Idiomatic Python. A feel for what’s natural to Python users. APIs that free users rather than constrain them.Compilers. The path from authoring to kernels (IR, lowering, optimization), weighed against maintainability.And how you work: proactive and largely self-directed. You fetch context across the company instead of waiting for it. You’re comfortable talking to the engineers who use what you build, and at ease designing in the open for users you’ll never meet. Ready to grow into leading a small team (a couple of people, near term).What great looks likePeople adopt Quadrants from outside Genesis. Engineers write clearer code with less boilerplate. Kernels keep getting faster. Performance is tracked, not guessed. The architecture gets easier to extend, not harder.What we’re uncompromising aboutHow you work is up to you. You read and challenge the codebase instead of just stacking features on it. You take nothing you did not write for granted. You watch the competition and what’s coming next, and you bring it in and ship it.Use AI agents if they help. They are productivity tools, not code owners.
