That means bringing information together from different systems, recording transactions correctly, preparing useful reports, and helping people understand what needs their attention.Today, much of this work depends on spreadsheets, repeated data entry and people checking one system against another. Our ambition is to make that work increasingly automatic, while keeping every number explainable and every consequential action under clear control.We are building towards a complete business management system for growing companies. These founding roles will shape both the product and the way we build it.About the roleYou will own how customers experience Agent F, from landing pages and product demonstrations through onboarding and migration to the work they do every day. A founder looking at their finances for the first time and a controller investigating a discrepancy need different levels of detail. Both should understand where they are, what a number means and what to do next.This combines product design with hands-on front-end engineering. You will talk to customers, shape the journey, design the interactions and ship them in the product. You will use AI coding agents to help implement changes, and take responsibility for reviewing the code and checking the finished experience.Your work will connect the product into a coherent whole: consistent navigation, familiar controls and clear explanations across features. You will also own the steps that turn an interested visitor into an active, paying customer.What you will build and improveAn engaging path from first interest to a useful result. Connect landing pages and product demonstrations to sign-up, account setup and the first session so a customer understands what to provide and what they will get back. Measure where people abandon the process and address the causes.A migration experience people can follow. Help customers bring in their history from accounting software or spreadsheets. Make upload progress, missing information, validation errors and next steps understandable.A consistent product experience. Develop the design language, navigation and reusable components used across the product. Make tables, forms and reports behave predictably, including loading, empty and error states.Useful decision screens. Design views that help customers compare recommendations, understand costs and choose what happens next. Our planned evidence board brings this information together as customers describe their needs.Interfaces that earn trust. Help users see where a figure came from, understand a proposed change and review it before approval. Include accessibility, keyboard use and clear language in the implementation.Improvements grounded in actual use. Keep up with the customer pipeline, from interested prospects to customers onboarding or migrating. Observe customer sessions and work with the customer-facing team. Turn recurring questions into product changes, then check whether those changes helped.For example, a customer uploads a file and sees a different total from the one they expected. You would design the journey that explains what was imported, what needs checking and how to resolve the difference, working with the data engineer on the underlying evidence.What you bringYou have five or more years of experience designing and shipping software, including business-to-business software sold as a service (B2B SaaS). You may come from product design with strong engineering skills, or from front-end engineering with substantial design ownership.You can show a product journey you improved, explain the choices you made and describe the effect on customers. You have owned an onboarding, activation or conversion measure: whether people got started, reached a useful result or became paying customers.Core experienceProduct design across information architecture, interaction design and visual design.Production front-end work with React, TypeScript, CSS and reusable components, including reviewing and debugging code generated by agents.Building or maintaining a design system that other people use.Customer research, usability testing and product analytics that inform what you ship.Daily use of AI coding agents, with a clear approach to specifications, review and verification.Clear written explanations of design decisions and their trade-offs.Useful additional experienceFinancial software, complex tables and dashboards, or products where people need to inspect the source of a result. Experience with configuration-driven interfaces, where shared rules and data determine how a screen is assembled, would also be useful.What early progress could look likeIn your first months, you would map the main customer journeys, establish a baseline for onboarding and conversion, and ship an improvement to a step where customers regularly get stuck. Alongside that, you would start consolidating repeated interface patterns into reusable components.We would look for evidence that customers reach a useful result sooner, complete more of the journey independently and need less help with the interface. The exact priorities will follow the customer needs you find with the team.Operational excellence and customer commitmentsYou take pride in a product customers can depend on under pressure. When sign-up, migration or a critical financial workflow breaks, you step in, establish what the customer needs and work with the team to restore a safe path forward. A misleading balance, missing transaction or incorrect status can be a financial emergency even when the page loads normally. You make the problem visible, help contain its impact and verify the complete customer journey after a fix.Customer commitments shape how we work. You are willing to interrupt planned work, respond promptly and stay engaged when an urgent issue puts a service-level agreement (SLA), onboarding commitment or financial deadline at risk. That requires flexibility beyond normal working hours as part of agreed on-call coverage and coordinated incident response. You keep people informed and see the issue through to a verified recovery or an explicit handover. Afterwards, you improve the system so the same emergency becomes less likely.How you will workThis is a senior founding role in a small team, with scope to shape product decisions and engineering practice. You will work closely with the engineers responsible for platform operations and customer data. You will carry work from customer observation through implementation and release, then follow up on how it performs.Everyone shares responsibility for the whole product and the customer outcome. You will pick up the most important work or whatever is on fire, including tasks outside your specialty. You take initiative, bring in the right expertise and stay involved until the problem is resolved. Customer impact and urgency determine where you focus.The role is full-time and in-person in Berlin. German is not required.Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

PCB design experience, including schematic capture, component selection, layout review, prototype bring-up, and verification.

description_clean: In just over two years, we’ve gone from 0 to over 900 customers, succeeding where many have tried and failed before. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we’re having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and have been scaling the team to massively grow our impact. You build trust through high standards and shared success.Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Forward-Deployed Engineer
description_clean:
Tangible Markets builds secondary-transaction infrastructure for private markets. Our clients are banks, fund administrators, and secondaries teams whose workflows are technical, regulated, and specific. You sit between them and our product engineering.
The role blends solutions engineering with customer success, plus real engineering work. You lead technical discussions with clients, shape how the platform fits their workflow, own their success after go-live, and help build configurations and integrations that close the gap. You are not embedded on client sites full-time, and this is not a pure relationship role either. Most weeks split between client-facing work and hands-on technical work.
Full-time · Remote (European time zones preferred)
Tasks
Client-facing (roughly half the role)

Run technical discussions during onboarding: architecture reviews, security questionnaires, SSO and data-flow conversations with client IT teams
Translate client workflow requirements into product terms, and product capabilities into client terms
Own accounts after go-live: adoption, expansion, the quarterly “how is this actually going” conversation
Be the trusted technical contact when something breaks or a new requirement lands

Product and engineering (the other half)

Help build client-specific configuration, integrations, and glue code (SSO, data mappings, API integrations, etc.)
Turn recurring client asks into structured product requirements and argue for them with the product team
Prototype solutions fast, validate them with the client, then hand the generalizable parts to the engineering team
Write the runbooks and docs that make each client’s setup maintainable by someone other than you

Requirements

3+ years in a technical role with client exposure: solutions engineering, sales engineering, technical account management, or product engineering with heavy customer contact.
You can read and write production code: You don’t need to be the strongest or only engineer on the team, but “I’ll build it” has to be a real option, not a handoff.
You can hold a room: an SSO deep-dive with a bank’s IT security team in the morning, a product feedback session in the afternoon.
Financial services background, or evidence you absorb regulated domains fast.
You write clearly: Requirement docs, runbooks, and follow-up emails carry most of this job’s leverage.
Judgment about what to build, what to configure, and what to push back on.

Nice to have:

Anything fintech, especially on the vendor for banks (or other fintechs) side.
Prior work at an early-stage B2B company where you wore several hats.
Familiarity with enterprise security and compliance processes (vendor due diligence, DORA, GDPR).

What this role is not:

Not pre-sales quota-carrying. You join conversations for technical depth, not to close.
Not full-time on-site embedding. Client contact is regular but structured: calls, workshops.
Not a support queue. You own outcomes for accounts, not tickets.

Why this role matters:
Enterprise clients in private markets churn because nobody on the vendor side understood their workflow well enough to make the platform fit. This role exists so that someone does, and so that what they learn changes the product.
Process:

30-minute intro call
Technical conversation around a real (anonymized) client scenario
Working session: scope a solution and present it back
Conversation with the founders
